tasks.short: Read the referral and medical data, test the patient's physical and mental abilities, score the tests, set realistic rehabilitation goals with the patient, and record them.

steps.what: Occupational therapist reads the referral and analyzes medical data
Occupational therapist tests and evaluates the patient's physical and mental abilities
Occupational therapist scores the assessment forms by hand
Occupational therapist determines realistic rehabilitation goals with the patient
Occupational therapist writes the goals in the record

tasks.design: The record ({OTHER}) shows diagnosis, medication, earlier therapy and the referral question in one view. Standard assessments are filled on a tablet form in the record, which computes the scores by the published rules instead of hand scoring. Goals are entered in a structured goal template linked to the scores; the therapist still writes each goal. Testing the patient and setting goals together stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medical data were spread over screens and tests scored by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records hold assessment forms that score by fixed rules.
tasks.still_hard: Some assessments are licensed only on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Setting a goal that matters to the patient, not only to the therapist.

reach.learn: Whether goals and scores are in the record on the day.

evidence.claim: Records can hold assessment forms that compute scores by fixed rules.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to goals recorded; treatment is outside.
Input contract: assessment licences allow digital forms; fallback is paper scoring.
Testing and goal setting stay with the therapist.
Patients' time does not change.

s1 keeps 75: reading and analysing stay; paging through screens goes. s3 keeps 20 because scores are computed by the published rules and the therapist checks them. s5 keeps 85: the template fills scores and layout, but each goal is the therapist's own first record. Filling the tablet form during testing takes about the time paper took, so s2 keeps 100.

incremental.description: Occupational therapist enters scores of paper-only tests.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: test licences do not allow digital forms, so scoring stays by hand (s3 keeps 100) and the view misses data (s1 keeps 90) (2.5); high: standard digital assessments as designed (12.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write treatment notes after sessions, record measurements, write progress reports to referrers, check them, send them, and register treatments for billing.

steps.what: Occupational therapist writes treatment notes to complete and maintain records: typed today; after the change spoken as a short summary that a scribe turns into a draft

loop.input: The therapist's spoken summary after the session and the patient's goals in the record.
loop.output: A draft treatment note in the record's format.
loop.check: A validator flags any goal, measurement or risk statement that does not match the record; the therapist reads the draft against what happened in the session and the spoken summary, corrects it, and types the note when the draft misses or changes a point, before it is saved.
loop.stop: One draft per session; if the therapist rejects it, they type the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sessions vary; a fixed form does not capture what happened.

steps.what: Occupational therapist records measurements and scores in the record
Occupational therapist writes progress reports to referrers
Occupational therapist checks the final report: progress, measurements and advice match the record and its limits, and the addressee is the referrer
Occupational therapist sends the checked report to the referrer: by e-mail today, by one release through the secure care exchange after the change
Occupational therapist registers treatments for billing: by hand today; after the change codes follow from the appointment type by fixed rules and the therapist checks them against the sessions held

tasks.design: After a session, the therapist speaks a short summary and a scribe drafts the treatment note; a validator flags goals, measurements and risk statements that do not match the record, and the therapist approves before saving. Measurements are entered on a tablet form during the session; this first record keeps its time. Progress reports are drafted from the record and checked against it; the therapist checks the report and releases it to the referrer through the secure care exchange. Billing codes follow from the agenda appointment type by fixed rules. Sessions are not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes, reports and billing were typed by hand after sessions.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes the clinician validates; records derive billing from appointments.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add statements the therapist did not make.
tasks.human_edge: Writing what a referrer needs to know about a patient's home situation.
tasks.altitude: The therapist validates drafts instead of typing.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts the note and the clinician validates it before it goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session held to treatments registered; insurer processing is outside.
Input contract: goals and scores in the record; fallback is typing.
The therapist approves every note and report.
A DPIA and works council consent come before use.
s3 is part of preparing progress reports, which sibling task 29-1122.00:348 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.

s1 keeps 80: speaking a summary is quicker than typing, but the note is still the therapist's own record and every draft is read. s2 is a first record and keeps its full time. s5 keeps 10 for the release. s6 keeps 30 for checking the codes.
research_questions: How long does the therapist spend editing drafts?

incremental.description: No new work: speaking the summary replaces typing and is inside s1.

approvals.approved_version: The progress report exactly as checked by the therapist in s4, sent once to the named referrer through the secure care exchange; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts from short summaries need heavy edits, so s1 keeps 90, and the code rules miss many appointment types, so s6 keeps 60 (14.5); high: drafts and rules as designed (23.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the therapy program, conduct therapy sessions, schedule sessions with patients, arrange aids and materials, and coordinate with the care team.

steps.what: Occupational therapist plans and organizes the occupational therapy program
Occupational therapist schedules sessions with patients: by phone today; after the change opens slots and phones only patients who cannot book online
Patient books follow-up sessions in the patient portal from the open slots
Occupational therapist conducts therapy sessions to help rehabilitate persons with disabilities
Occupational therapist prepares aid and material requests: by e-mail today; on the supplier's ordering portal with the patient's measurements filled from the record after the change
Occupational therapist checks the final request: the aid fits the patient's needs and measurements, and it goes to the right supplier
Occupational therapist submits the checked request to the supplier
Occupational therapist coordinates with the care team

tasks.design: Patients book follow-up sessions in the patient portal from the slots the therapist opens in the agenda ({CALENDAR}) and get text reminders, so fewer bookings are made by phone. Aids are requested on the supplier's ordering portal with the patient's measurements filled from the record; the therapist checks and submits each request. Planning the program, conducting sessions and coordinating with the team stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sessions were booked by phone and aids requested by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Agendas offer online booking and reminders; aid suppliers take portal orders.
tasks.still_hard: Patients with cognitive problems need phone booking.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting an exercise when the patient is in pain that day.

evidence.claim: Agendas can offer online booking with text reminders; aid suppliers can take portal orders.

assumptions: Boundary: from the goals to the team coordinated; discharge is outside.
Input contract: supplier portals available; fallback is phone and e-mail.

Patients book online (s2b, share 1, customer time) in about the time a call took. s2 keeps 40 for opening slots and phoning patients who cannot book online. s4 keeps 50 for choosing the aid and answering supplier questions; the check (s4b) and the submission (s4c) take 1 each.
Sessions do not change.

incremental.description: Occupational therapist opens booking slots in the agenda.

approvals.approved_version: The aid request with item and the patient's measurements exactly as checked by the therapist in s4b, submitted once to the named supplier; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of patients still book by phone, so s2 keeps 70, and few suppliers have a portal, so s4 keeps 80 (3.8); high: most patients book online and portals for most aids (8.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan skills programs and social activities, lead them, arrange placements with employers and schools, and track attendance and progress.

steps.what: Occupational therapist plans programs and social activities to help patients learn work or school skills
Occupational therapist leads activities and skills training
Occupational therapist arranges placements with employers and schools
Occupational therapist tracks attendance and progress in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Attendance and goal scores per participant are ticked on a group list in the record ({OTHER}) during the activity, replacing the separate spreadsheet. Planning programs, leading activities and arranging placements stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance and progress were kept in a spreadsheet beside the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Records have group modules with attendance and goal scores.
tasks.still_hard: Progress in social skills is hard to score.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a young patient through a first day at a work placement.

evidence.claim: Records can hold group modules with attendance and goal scores.

assumptions: Boundary: from patient goals to progress tracked; placement contracts are outside.
Input contract: group module in the record; fallback is a spreadsheet.
Planning, leading and arranging do not change.
Patients' time does not change.
s4 keeps 60: ticking attendance and goal scores per participant is a first record and stays; keeping a separate spreadsheet next to the record goes.
research_questions: Is progress per participant recorded more often?

incremental.description: Occupational therapist sets up a group list for each new program.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the group module is not used for most programs, so the spreadsheet stays and s4 keeps 90 (0.5); high: group lists in the record as designed (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The occupational therapist keeps testing, setting goals, treating and leading activities; hand scoring, typed notes and phone bookings shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time for patients.
